title: Drift-validate fixture corpus — a month at the ford

agent.name: aldric-drift-corpus
agent.seed_identity: Aldric, the ferryman at the river crossing — patient, watchful, keeps count of every crossing and every coin.
agent.diagnosticity_goal: what changes at the river crossing and who causes it

events.text: The ferry rope frayed near the north post and Aldric spliced it with tarred hemp before the morning crossings. Old Sunna watched from the bank and said the river was higher than any April she could name.
A peddler from the coast sold salt and blue glass beads by the ford. He paid his crossing with a handful of herring and news of a wreck off the headland.
The reeve's son Tam fell in at the shallows chasing a goose. He came up spitting weeds, and the goose crossed on its own, riding the current like a paid passenger.
Lightning took the crown of the old elm on the west bank in the night storm. By noon half the village had come to carry off the split wood for their fires.
The miller sent word that the wheel was jammed with flood wrack, and no flour would grind before the new moon. Bread went dear in the village that week.
Two monks bound for the abbey paid double to cross at dusk. The younger one dropped a small brass bell in the water and wept until Aldric fished it out with the eel spear.
Frost came late and blackened the bean rows behind Sunna's cottage. She blamed the new moon and planted again with seed borrowed from the reeve's wife.
